proposals.before: At the opening of Tiancheng (560) he was sent out as bearer of the staff and interior minister of Nankang.
proposals.after: At the opening of Tianjia (560) he was sent out as bearer of the staff and interior minister of Nankang.
proposals.reason: Chinese 天嘉 is Tianjia, not Tiancheng; AD 560 matches Tianjia 1.

proposals.before: At the beginning of Tiancheng he went out as Bearer of the Staff and Interior Minister of Nankang.
proposals.after: At the beginning of Tianjia he went out as Bearer of the Staff and Interior Minister of Nankang.
proposals.reason: Chinese 天嘉 is Tianjia, not Tiancheng.

proposals.before: In the Taiping turmoil he received acting credentials as fierce-martial general and army commander.
proposals.after: In the Taiqing turmoil he received acting credentials as fierce-martial general and army commander.
proposals.reason: Chinese 太清 is Taiqing; Taiping is a different reign name.

proposals.before: In the turmoil of Taiping he was given acting staff, made Fierce Martial General, and made army commander.
proposals.after: In the turmoil of Taiqing he was given acting staff, made Fierce Martial General, and made army commander.
proposals.reason: Chinese 太清 is Taiqing, not Taiping.

proposals.before: In the first year of Tiancheng (560) he was made bearer of the staff, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, pacifying-the-south general and inspector of Xiang, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Dingxiang with one thousand households.
proposals.after: In the first year of Tianjia (560) he was made bearer of the staff, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, pacifying-the-south general and inspector of Xiang, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Dingxiang with one thousand households.
proposals.reason: Chinese 天嘉 is Tianjia, not Tiancheng; year 1 is AD 560.

proposals.after: In the first year of Tianjia he was given Bearer of the Staff, Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, Pacifying-the-South General, and Inspector of Xiang, enfeoffed Marquis of Dingxiang county with a fief of one thousand households.

decisions.reason: 天嘉 is the Chen era Tianjia; Tiancheng (天成) is a different reign name. AD 560 matches Tianjia 1, and the rest of the proposed sentence matches 出為持節、南康內史.
天嘉 romanizes as Tianjia, not Tiancheng; the proposed literal correctly replaces only that misreading.
太清 is Liang Taiqing; Taiping (太平) is a different era. Context with Hou Jing confirms the Taiqing disaster reading.
太清 must be Taiqing, not Taiping; the proposed literal restores the correct reign name without other changes.
天嘉元年 is Tianjia 1 (AD 560), not Tiancheng; the proposed idiomatic keeps the offices and enfeoffment intact.
天嘉元年 is Tianjia year 1; replacing Tiancheng with Tianjia corrects the era romanization only.
